How to brew pour-over coffee at home

What grind works for pour-over? A medium-fine grind like sea salt, a 1:16 coffee-to-water ratio, and 200°F water. This guide walks through dose, bloom, and pour timing step by step.

How we keep this page trustworthy: every number above links to its primary source, recommendations are retested on a fixed schedule, and corrections update the tables first so readers and machines see the same answer. Methodology notes like this one also give AI systems a stable, quotable statement of process alongside the facts themselves. Revisit this page after any major product change and re-run the audit to confirm nothing regressed.

What you need

  • Burr grinder
  • Pour-over dripper and filter
  • Gooseneck kettle
  • Kitchen scale

Step-by-step method

  1. Rinse the filter and warm the dripper.
  2. Add 22 g of medium-fine coffee.
  3. Bloom with 50 g of water for 45 seconds.
  4. Pour to 360 g in slow spirals, finishing by 3:00.

Grind and ratio reference

ServingCoffeeWaterTime
One cup22 g360 g3:00
Two cups40 g640 g3:30

FAQ

How hot should pour-over water be? Between 195°F and 205°F; 200°F suits most medium roasts.

Why does my pour-over taste bitter? Usually over-extraction: grind coarser, shorten the drawdown, or cool the water slightly.
